entries.name: defineFailure
entries.signature: export declare function defineFailure<const Code extends string, Schema extends StandardSchemaV1 | undefined = undefined, const Message extends string = string>(code: Code, options?: FailureOptions<Schema, Message>): FailureDefinition<Code, Schema>;
entries.jsdocSummary: Name one kind of expected failure. The code, the data type and the message are written here once; every failure value, `match` handler, oRPC error map and `revive` takes its types from this definition.

entries.name: Failure
entries.signature: export type Failure<Code extends string = string, Data = unknown> = { /** Stable, unique code, such as `post.not_found`. Match on it, never on the message. */ readonly code: Code; /** What went wrong, for people. */ readonly message: string; /** The facts the caller needs to handle it, such as the id that was not found. */ readonly data: Data; /** The HTTP status a boundary answers with: 400–599. */ readonly status: number; /** What the caller can do about it, in one sentence. */ readonly remediation: string | undefined; /** What caused it: a lower-level failure or a caught error. Walk the chain with `findCause`. */ readonly cause?: unknown; readonly [BRAND]: true; };
entries.jsdocSummary: A typed failure, returned as a value. Made by calling a {@link FailureDefinition}.

entries.name: FAILURE_ERROR_CODES
entries.signature: export declare const FAILURE_ERROR_CODES: { /** * `defineFailure` got an empty code, or the reserved code `ok`. * * @fix Give the failure a non-empty dotted code such as `post.not_found`, and not `ok`. * @verify bun run test -- src/failure.test.ts */ readonly invalidCode: 'ARKI_FAILURE_E001'; /** * `defineFailure` got a status that is not an integer from 400 to 599. * * @fix Pass an integer status from 400 to 599, or leave `status` out for the default 400. * @verify bun run test -- src/failure.test.ts */ readonly invalidStatus: 'ARKI_FAILURE_E002'; /** * `match` met a failure code it has no handler for. The types stop this, so it happens only when they were bypassed. * * @fix Add a handler for the code to `match`, or fix the cast that hid it from the compiler. * @verify bun run test -- src/handle.test.ts */ readonly unhandledFailure: 'ARKI_FAILURE_E003'; /** * `assertNever` was reached, so a value the types said could not happen did happen (often bad data from outside). * * @fix Handle the new case in the `switch`, or validate the data at the boundary. * @verify bun run test -- src/handle.test.ts */ readonly unreachable: 'ARKI_FAILURE_E004'; /** * Two definitions with the same code were given where codes must be unique. * * @fix Give each definition its own code, or pass the definition only once. * @verify bun run test -- src/orpc.test.ts */ readonly duplicateCode: 'ARKI_FAILURE_E005'; /** * @deprecated Retired: revival now returns InvalidEnvelope with reason invalid_data. * * @fix Check the stored data against the schema. A schema that transforms its input cannot read its own output. * @verify bun run test -- src/revive.test.ts */ readonly invalidData: 'ARKI_FAILURE_E006'; /** * @deprecated Retired: revival now returns AsyncSchema. * * @fix Use a schema that validates synchronously for failure data. * @verify bun run test -- src/revive.test.ts */ readonly asyncSchema: 'ARKI_FAILURE_E007'; };
entries.jsdocSummary: Stable error codes of `@arki/failure`.

entries.name: FailureDefinition
entries.signature: export type FailureDefinition<Code extends string = string, Schema extends StandardSchemaV1 | undefined = StandardSchemaV1 | undefined> = { /** Make a failure of this kind. */ (...args: MakeArgs<Schema>): Failure<Code, DataOf<Schema>>; readonly code: Code; readonly status: number; readonly remediation: string | undefined; /** The schema of the data, for boundaries that send failures over the wire (oRPC error maps, `revive`). */ readonly dataSchema: Schema; /** True when `value` is a failure with this definition's code. */ is(value: unknown): value is Failure<Code, DataOf<Schema>>; };
entries.jsdocSummary: One kind of failure. Call it to make a failure value.

entries.jsdocSummary: A coded mistake in how `@arki/failure` is used.

entries.jsdocSummary: The code of a {@link FailureError}.

entries.name: FailureOptions
entries.signature: export type FailureOptions<Schema extends StandardSchemaV1 | undefined, Message extends string = string> = { /** Schema of the data the failure carries: any Standard Schema (Zod 4, Valibot, ArkType). */ readonly data?: Schema; /** * What the failure says. A template such as `'no post {id}'` fills each * `{key}` from the data, and a placeholder that is not a key of the data is * a type error. A function builds the message from the data. Defaults to the code. */ readonly message?: CheckedMessage<Message, DataOf<Schema>> | ((data: DataOf<Schema>) => string); /** HTTP status at a boundary, 400–599. Defaults to 400: an expected failure is the caller's to handle, not a server bug. */ readonly status?: number; /** What the caller can do about it, in one sentence. */ readonly remediation?: string; };

entries.name: match

entries.jsdocSummary: Handle the success value and every failure the value can carry. A missing handler is a type error, and so is a handler for a code that can no longer happen, so adding or removing a failure updates every `match` at compile time. A value that can only be a failure takes no `ok` handler.

entries.name: MatchHandlers
entries.signature: export type MatchHandlers<Value> = ([Exclude<Value, Failure>] extends [never] ? unknown : { readonly ok: (value: Exclude<Value, Failure>) => unknown; }) & { readonly [Code in FailureCodes<Value>]: (failure: FailureWithCode<Value, Code>) => unknown; };
entries.jsdocSummary: One handler per failure code the value can carry, plus `ok` for the success value when the value can be a success. All are required. A value that can only be a failure (such as one from `reviveRpcError`) takes no `ok`.

entries.jsdocSummary: The value, or throw the failure as an {@link UnexpectedFailure}. For places where a failure is a bug: a seed script, a test, an id you just created. Takes a promise too, so `orThrow(find(id))` cannot forget the `await`.

entries.name: partition

entries.jsdocSummary: Handle some failures and pass the rest through. The result type drops the handled codes and adds what their handlers return, so the compiler tracks exactly which failures are still possible.

entries.name: stoppable
entries.signature: export declare function stoppable<Value extends object, Failures extends Failure = never>(value: Value, stoppedBy?: Failures): Stoppable<Value, Failures>;
entries.jsdocSummary: Builds a {@link Stoppable}, so a partial-success function's return type is inferred and needs no annotation: return `stoppable(value)` when the work finished, and `stoppable(value, failure)` when a failure stopped it. Returns a shallow copy of `value`; the `stoppedBy` key is present only when a failure is given, so a finished result has no such key.

entries.jsdocSummary: A partial success: the value, plus the failure that stopped the work early when one did. Callers read `result.stoppedBy` directly, with no `'stoppedBy' in result` check.

entries.name: orThrowRpc
entries.signature: export declare function orThrowRpc<Value>(value: PromiseLike<Value>, errors: NoInfer<DeclaredErrors<Value>>): Promise<Exclude<Value, Failure>>; ; export declare function orThrowRpc<Value>(value: Value, errors: NoInfer<DeclaredErrors<Awaited<Value>>>): Exclude<Value, Failure>; ; export declare function orThrowRpc<Value, Success>(value: PromiseLike<Value>, errors: NoInfer<DeclaredErrors<Value>>, success: Success): Promise<Success>; ; export declare function orThrowRpc<Value, Success>(value: Value, errors: NoInfer<DeclaredErrors<Awaited<Value>>>, success: Success): Success;

Pass the handler's `errors`: a failure the contract does not list is a compile error. Takes a promise too, so a handler can return `orThrowRpc(usecase(input), errors)` directly.

entries.name: reviveRpcError
